text: In those days, when again a large crowd had gathered and had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to him and said,
"I have compassion on the crowd. They have been with me three days now and have nothing to eat.
If I send them home hungry, they will collapse on the way — and some of them have come a long distance."
His disciples answered, "Where out here in this wilderness could anyone find enough bread to feed them?"
He asked them, "How many loaves do you have?" "Seven," they said.
So he told the crowd to sit down on the ground. Taking the seven loaves, he gave thanks, broke them, and gave them to his disciples to distribute, and they set them before the crowd.
They also had a few small fish. He blessed them as well and told the disciples to distribute them too.
The people ate and were satisfied, and the disciples gathered up seven baskets of leftover pieces.
There were about four thousand present. Then he sent them away,
and immediately got into the boat with his disciples and went to the district of Dalmanutha.
The Pharisees came out and began to argue with him, demanding a sign from heaven to test him.
He sighed deeply in his spirit and said, "Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation."

versions.text: He sighed deeply and said, "Why does this generation demand a sign? Truly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation."
versions.explanation: The phrase "in his spirit" (τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ) is omitted; it underscores the depth of Jesus' inner reaction and reads well aloud.

text: Then he left them, got back into the boat, and crossed to the other side.
The disciples had forgotten to bring bread; they had only one loaf with them in the boat.
He warned them, "Watch out — beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod."
They said to one another, "It's because we have no bread."
Aware of this, Jesus said to them, "Why are you talking about having no bread? Do you still not perceive or understand? Are your hearts hardened?
You have eyes — don't you see? You have ears — don't you hear? Don't you remember?
When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets full of pieces did you gather?" "Twelve," they told him.

versions.text: When I broke the five loaves for the five thousand, how many baskets of pieces did you gather?" "Twelve," they told him.
versions.explanation: The Greek specifies baskets "full" (πλήρεις) of pieces; the emphasis on abundance is lost in "baskets of pieces."

text: "And when I broke the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets of pieces did you gather?" "Seven," they said.
And he said to them, "Do you still not understand?"
They came to Bethsaida, and people brought a blind man to Jesus and begged Jesus to touch him.

versions.text: They came to Bethsaida, and people brought a blind man to Jesus and begged him to touch him.
versions.explanation: The chain of pronouns ("begged him to touch him") is ambiguous when read aloud; naming Jesus once clarifies who is being asked.

text: He took the blind man by the hand and led him outside the village. Then he spit on the man's eyes, laid his hands on him, and asked, "Do you see anything?"
The man looked up and said, "I see people — they look like trees walking around."
Then Jesus laid his hands on the man's eyes again. The man looked intently, his sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.

versions.text: Then Jesus laid his hands on the man's eyes again. His sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
versions.explanation: The first verb (διέβλεψεν, "he looked intently" / "opened his eyes wide") is dropped; the Greek has three stages of the healing, which the restored reading preserves.

text: Jesus sent him home, saying, "Don't even go into the village."
Jesus and his disciples went on to the villages around Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked them, "Who do people say I am?"
They answered, "John the Baptist; others say Elijah; and still others, one of the prophets."
"But what about you?" he asked. "Who do you say I am?" Peter answered, "You are the Christ."
And he ordered them not to tell anyone about him.
Then he began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
He spoke about this quite openly. Then Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him.
But Jesus turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter: "Get behind me, Satan! You do not have in mind the things of God, but the things of men."

versions.text: But Jesus turned, looked at his disciples, and rebuked Peter: "Get behind me, Satan! You are not thinking the thoughts of God, but of men."
versions.explanation: "Thinking the thoughts of God" is an awkward and slightly misleading rendering of φρονεῖς τὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, which means setting one's mind on God's concerns rather than human ones.

text: Then he called the crowd to him along with his disciples and said, "Whoever wants to come after me must deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake and for the gospel will save it.
What good is it for a person to gain the whole world and forfeit his life?
Or what can anyone give in exchange for his life?
If anyone is ashamed of me and my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his Father's glory with the holy angels."
